facts.statement: Bathytheristes is an extinct genus of chimaera that lived during the late Early Jurassic epoch.
facts.quote: Bathytheristes is an extinct genus of chimaera from the late Early Jurassic epoch of the Jurassic Period.

facts.statement: The fossil of Bathytheristes was discovered in the Posidonia Shale Formation at Ohmden, Germany.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the early Toarcian-aged Posidonia Shale Formation of Ohmden, Germany.

facts.statement: The name Bathytheristes roughly translates to "Reaper of the deep."
facts.quote: Its name roughly translates to "Reaper of the deep."

facts.statement: Bathytheristes is known from only one species, Bathytheristes gracilis.
facts.quote: It is known from a single species, B. gracilis.

facts.statement: The specific epithet gracilis refers to the slender nature of the tooth plate in this species.
facts.quote: The specific epithet refers to the slender of the tooth plate in this species.

facts.statement: Bathytheristes is related to the modern elephantfish.
facts.quote: It is related to the modern elephantfish.

facts.statement: Bathytheristes belongs to the parent group Callorhinchidae.
Bathytheristes is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Bathytheristes lived between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago during the Toarcian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)
